drug_class: Blood volume expander / plasma protein replacement
purpose: Albumin Human is used to replace a protein in your blood called albumin, which helps keep fluid in the right places in your body. It is often given when you have low blood protein levels due to conditions like liver disease, burns, surgery, or serious illness. It can also help restore blood volume when you have lost a lot of fluid or blood.
how_it_works: Albumin is a natural protein normally made by your liver that travels through your bloodstream. It acts like a sponge, pulling and holding fluid inside your blood vessels so it does not leak into your tissues and cause swelling. When your albumin levels are too low, giving you this medicine through an IV helps bring those levels back up and keeps your blood pressure and fluid balance stable.
common_side_effects: Chills, fever, flushing, nausea, low blood pressure, increased heart rate, headache, rash or itching, and a feeling of warmth. Most of these are mild and happen during or shortly after the IV infusion.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have heart failure, kidney problems, severe anemia, or are allergic to any blood products, as albumin may not be safe for you. It is given only by a healthcare professional in a medical setting, and your heart, blood pressure, and fluid levels will be monitored closely. In rare cases, it can cause a serious allergic reaction — tell your nurse right away if you have trouble breathing, chest tightness, or severe dizziness during the infusion.
typical_dosing: Albumin is given through an IV in a hospital or clinic — you will not take it at home. The dose and how fast it is given depends on your condition, weight, and why you need it. Your doctor will decide the right amount for you, and a nurse will monitor you throughout the infusion.
